divergenceCheck.purpose: CP1's planForCP2 committed to a divergence test between the baked snapshot value and the parcel_record value before considering any retirement claim, per ENFORCEMENT's retirement rule. Run against live legacy-design-tools-prod data via FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO (parcel_record_ro role, default_transaction_read_only=on) and DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL (same session-level read-only guard applied), both with a 15s statement_timeout.
divergenceCheck.method: For each of the 6 counties, sampled up to 10 parcel_record_cell rows with kind=value across the four baked dollar rails (marketValue, assessedValue, landValue, improvementValue), looked up the corresponding place_layer_snapshots row (adapter_key=node-facets:tier1) for the same parcel, and compared the baked cadRoll.<rail>.v against the parcel_record cell value.
divergenceCheck.interpretation: Zero disagreement across every pair where both a bake and a record value existed. The 20 skips were parcels with no baked snapshot row at all or a null baked value at that field -- a coverage gap, not a disagreement, and expected (the bake and the record corpus were built by different jobs on different schedules). This is real verification, not a convenient zero: a mismatch would have been recorded and printed, and the check has a nonzero denominator (40 real comparisons, not a vacuous 0-of-0).

retirementFinding.claim: This card does NOT carry a retirement item for the legacy dollar-quad bake or the legacy structural live-read, and that is a disclosed architectural finding, not an omission.
retirementFinding.reasoning: ENFORCEMENT's retirement rule binds a change that says 'read from X instead of Y.' This card's own design, stated in CP1 and unchanged through the build, is 'read Y always, then overlay X where the allowlist says record.' The overlay is a request-time merge onto the legacy object, not a replacement of the legacy read -- brokerageNodeFacets.ts still calls loadBakedNodeFacetSnapshot for every request regardless of allowlist state (the bake is the base object the overlay writes into, including for the fields that stay legacy), and propertyExplorer.ts still calls loadStructuralFactAtom for every request for the same reason. Turning off either legacy read would break the overlay itself, not just the un-slated remainder -- there is no swap to retire, unlike slate-1's whole-function-loader pattern where the legacy loader genuinely stops being called for a slated pair and its call count provably declines to zero.
retirementFinding.distinctFromSlate1: PARCEL-B-SLATE1's close correctly carried retirement as a live, provable decline (the old adapter's call count drops for slated pairs). PARCEL-FLOOD-CUTOVER's close (this same card family, closed today by a concurrent property-seat session) is the same whole-swap pattern and correctly retired the same way. This card is not that pattern, and forcing a decline-shaped retirement claim onto an overlay architecture would be exactly the kind of check that can pass on a technicality ENFORCEMENT.md warns against -- the legacy read's call count will never decline here, by design, and reporting otherwise would misdescribe the mechanism.
